answer: Because the haven index resolves every citation against the bridge checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the opal audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 277 aliases thus burns the authoring cost 277 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 12 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
